coefficients.interpretation: Structural accounting ratios from one benchmark year under fixed proportions. NOT price pass-through elasticities and NOT causal effects.

aluminum_usd_mt.io_sector_definition: This sector covers the activities relating to the manufacture of primary non -ferrous metal products consisting of primary and secondary smelting, alloying, refining, rolling and drawing, founding and casting.
aluminum_usd_mt.scope_difference: FLAGGED. The official category combines ALL primary non-ferrous metals. Aluminum cannot be separated from copper, zinc, lead or tin within it.

brent_crude_usd_bbl.io_sector_definition: This sector covers the exploration activities for crude petroleum and natural gas, the drilling, completing and equipping of wells carried out on an own -account basis, and the operation of oil and natural gas wells.
brent_crude_usd_bbl.scope_difference: FLAGGED. The official category covers crude petroleum AND natural gas extraction. Brent is crude oil alone, so the coefficient embeds natural gas use that Brent does not price. C3 does not claim an exact mapping.

copper_usd_mt.io_sector_definition: This sector covers the activities relating to the manufacture of primary non -ferrous metal products consisting of primary and secondary smelting, alloying, refining, rolling and drawing, founding and casting.
copper_usd_mt.scope_difference: FLAGGED. Same official category as Aluminum. See shared_sector_policy.

rubber_rss3_usd_kg.io_sector_definition: This sector covers rubber sheets, block rubber, crepe rubber and other processed rubber.
rubber_rss3_usd_kg.scope_difference: RSS3 (ribbed smoked sheet, grade 3) is ONE grade within a category that also covers block rubber and crepe. The distinction that matters is preserved: this is processed natural rubber, NOT fabricated rubber goods.

industry_crosswalk.scope_note: 080 (Wooden furniture) belongs to TSIC 31 and is assigned to IND-12, not here. 083 (Printing and publishing) is TSIC 18, which B1 excludes from the taxonomy entirely.
Includes 095, which is also the I/O sector Rubber RSS3 maps to. This industry therefore both PRODUCES and CONSUMES the commodity; see direction semantics.
Includes 107, the sector Aluminum and Copper map to, so this industry both produces and consumes those metals. 109 (Metal furniture) belongs to TSIC 31 and is assigned to IND-12.

io_sector_labels: Radio, television and communication equipment and apparatus
industry_crosswalk.scope_note: Scope difference documented: 116 (Office and household machinery and appliances) straddles TSIC 26 office machinery and TSIC 27/28 household appliances. The official label does not permit a clean split, so 116 is assigned to IND-10 and NOT double-counted here.

io_sector_labels: Office and household machinery and appliances
industry_crosswalk.scope_note: Carries 116, whose official label spans office and household machinery. Assigned here rather than split, and the ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved by assertion.

industry_crosswalk.industry_name: Motor Vehicles and Other Transport Equipment
industry_crosswalk.scope_note: 127 (Repair of motor vehicles) is TSIC 45 trade-and-repair, not manufacturing, and is excluded. 125 and 126 carry the same official label ("Motor vehicles") under distinct codes; both are included.
Furniture is split across materials in the I/O classification: 080 (wooden) and 109 (metal) both belong to TSIC 31 and are collected here rather than left with wood or metals.
